data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's causal mechanism overgeneralizes: it equates 'can communicate' with a single shared consensus mechanism that constitutes a correlated failure point. But a shared protocol standard does not entail a shared implementation; mutually interoperable nodes using diverse protocol implementations (e.g., different TLS stacks, different DNS resolvers) can communicate without a single bug or zero-day binding all of them. The target conflates interoperability with implementation monoculture, so its causal mechanism for why independence is 'almost always an illusion' does not follow from its own premise about shared protocols.
